exposure: Mode of delivery (normal vaginal delivery vs. elective caesarean section)
Newborns delivered by elective caesarean section
Newborns delivered by normal vaginal delivery
outcome: Peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) levels at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 minutes after birth
cohort: 200 healthy term newborns at a tertiary care center
finding: Newborns delivered vaginally had significantly higher SpO2 levels and reached SpO2 >90% faster than those delivered by elective caesarean section.
